elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 still binds our client: "the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products". The covenant is narrowed, not deleted, so the preferred position (no restriction at all) is not achieved. The drafter expressly targeted the fallback, which the playbook permits where the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection (HDI funds Site development/hosting and is paid from Net Sales).

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The open-ended language "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to ...)" is deleted; the restriction now reaches only "any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products", and "Deerskin Products" is a defined, bounded product set (Section 1.1: apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog, excluding closeout items and Joan Cook Catalog products). No residual "any competing business" or unbounded field-of-use hook remains.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 as revised opens "during the term of this Agreement and in no event for more than twelve (12) months", and Section 10.7 limits survival to Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 — Section 6.1 is not listed, so there is no post-term tail.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap: "and in no event for more than twelve (12) months". This overrides the indefinite exposure created by the Section 4.1 automatic one-year renewals, since the covenant cannot exceed twelve months regardless of how long the term runs.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Inserted parenthetical: "(which restriction shall not apply to the Company's internal development or any acquisition by or of the Company)" — the internal-development carve-out is operative, not merely promised in the comment.

Same inserted parenthetical carves out "any acquisition by or of the Company", covering both acquisitions we make and acquisitions of us, so an acquired business's competing activity does not breach Section 6.1.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all five fallback elements are met in operative language — named product scope (Deerskin Products only), during-term application with no survival under Section 10.7, an express twelve-month cap, and carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

Preferred level is not met and was not attempted: the covenant on the Company survives in narrowed form. That is an acceptable outcome under the playbook (fallback clauses are not redlined further), but the finding should not be described as reaching the preferred position.

Minimal: a single edit to Section 6.1 removes only the offending scope language ("substantially similar" products and the Wilson's/Excelled "companies similar to" list) and adds only the cap and the two carve-outs required by the fallback checklist. Section 4.1 and Section 10.7 are quoted for context but untouched, and Section 6.3 (which restricts HDI and benefits us) is correctly left alone.

Preserves intent: the Section 6.2 closeout-merchandise exception, HDI's exclusive right to use the "Deerskin" brand for the Site, the term/auto-renewal mechanics and the survival regime all remain intact and non-contradictory.

Optional polish, not a defect: "during the term of this Agreement and in no event for more than twelve (12) months" leaves the commencement point implicit. Consider "for the period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on the earlier of the end of the term and the date twelve (12) months after the Effective Date" to foreclose any argument that the cap resets on each renewal.
Comment is on-tone and accurately describes each operative change; it does not promise anything the redline fails to deliver.
